precepts.text: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone, in whom we grow into an holy temple; Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple with a literal stone and brought forth through his loins the stone that builds the temple we are.
precepts.point: Behold, I will bring forth my servant the Branch, and the stone laid before Joshua with seven eyes; the Branch and the stone are Christ.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Zerubbabel built the second temple, so he brought forth a literal stone with a foundation. That's the first level. But it is twofold: he also brought forth the other stone through his loins, to build up the temple which is us here in the room.

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: the chief corner stone, the headstone. “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: that's us. “In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.”

So we are that holy temple that Christ builds. Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple, and he brought forth the same stone and the same foundation, which is Christ, on whom we are built. Praise the Lord for that.

precepts.text: And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone. Meaning he is the leader, he is the commander.
precepts.point: And your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it. Watch what God says to all our people that join with Esau and the Arabs. Your agreement with our people in a hellish condition shall not stand. Meaning God is going to kill them. He is going to judge them.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Against the covenant with death, the Lord God lays something else: “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.” This stone is Christ, and Ephesians proves it: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.”

Christ himself is the chief corner stone. That means he is the leader; he is the commander. Read on: “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord.” The whole building, fitly framed together on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, grows into a holy temple in him.

So “he that believeth shall not make haste” means the one who builds on that stone will not be confounded. You will be delivered. You will be saved.

Everyone else has built on something else. Our people made a covenant with death, the white man and his philosophies, and an agreement with hell, keeping our people in a low state. They made lies their refuge, Christianity and democracy, and hid themselves under falsehood, thinking the overflowing scourge of judgment will not come to them. But the Lord lays judgment to the line and righteousness to the plummet; the hail sweeps away the refuge of lies at the second coming, at Armageddon, and the covenant with death is disannulled. Only what is built on the corner stone, Christ, stands.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Christ's body was the temple, and his temple today is us. Peter says “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house”, and Paul shows how that house grows: “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”. All the building is you and me. See that word growing: Peter just explained how we grow, by laying aside all malice, all guile, all hypocrisies, all evil speakings, and desiring the sincere milk of the word.

You know what fitly framed together means? Stones have to come together. Brothers, we must merge together. Whatever your position is, play that position. Don't try to change positions through deceit. A brother was demoted in New York for lying over a simple thing; when we ask, most of the time we already know the answer, and when the witnesses are called, the liar is put on front street and found not worthy of his rank. A stone full of guile does not fit in the frame.

“In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.” Wherever our congregation is, that is a spiritual house, the real temple, and God dwells in it through the Spirit. That is why Zerubbabel is our example: he got to his position not only for his fighting skills but because he was of noble character, understanding God's truth. We should not be deceitful, envious, hateful or filled with guile toward one another, but lively stones with zeal, passion and fire, built together into the house where God lives.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
In the days of the Maccabees, “many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” They consented to the religion of the Greeks, idolatry: they gave up what God told them to do and said, we are going to do what they want us to do. They profaned the sabbath and left the feast days, sacrificed swine's flesh and unclean beasts, left their children uncircumcised, and made their souls abominable, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.”

Paul reminds the Ephesians of exactly that: “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands”. Remember, back in the day, you were Gentiles. What is another word for Gentile? Hellenized Jews, Greeks.

Why were they called Uncircumcision? Because it was their fathers, back in the time of the Maccabees, who decided they were not going to circumcise their children. The Circumcision in the flesh were those whose fathers decided to stay, who did not give up, who did not allow their children to become Hellenized. Paul is telling them, remember: you were living like heathens. To the Corinthians he says the same: “ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.”

The racial slur this country put on our people is another form of that same Hellenization. The devil called us that. It is one of the most hateful epithets in the English language, and we took it up, changed the ending, and called it friendly and empowering. There is nothing empowering about it. Your oppressor named you that to demean you; you did not call yourself that. If you call someone that, you are telling them they are unrepentant, that they have fully learned the customs of the heathen, and that the Hellenization worked.

That was Esau's mission: to take away our heritage and make us something we are not, so that we forget the law. Brothers and sisters, we are not that word. We never have been, and Lord's will, we will never be again. When we come out of that mind frame, we do not refer to each other that way.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Has this happened yet? No. We are waiting on this second coming, waiting to be delivered again. That is why unification is so important: we have to go back to all these places, because our people are there. The Bible says they are in Assyria, in Egypt, in Pathros, in Cush, in Elam, and in the islands of the sea. We have a lot of work to do.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The outcasts are those who were kept afar off, living amongst the other nations as heathens, like Hellenized Jews. These are the ones Paul calls those “who sometimes were far off” and are now “made nigh by the blood of Christ.”

“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” The envy of Ephraim, the northern kingdom, is the wall of partition, and it is going to be gone. No more division: light skinned against dark skinned, look at your hair, look at my hair; the northern kingdom looking at us and us looking at them. Yes, Esau touched the northern kingdom; the southern kingdom has been through changes too. We look different today, but we are all the same people.

That wall is what Christ tore down. “He is our peace, who hath made both one”: the two sticks, Judah and Ephraim, made one, and right now in the congregation northern and southern kingdom are back together again.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Christ came and died for his people; he was cut off for his people. Romans 5:9 says we are “justified by his blood”, and Ephesians says it is that same blood that brings near those who were far off.

“For he is our peace, who hath made both one”. That is the peace of Romans 5:1, “we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ”. And it shows who is being spoken of. Who is the both? The two nations. When you read the history in the book of Kings, Israel and Judah split apart into two kingdoms, and Ezekiel prophesied that our king would come and die for the nation of Israel and the nation of Judah, so that they would no longer be two nations but one nation under Christ.

He “hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace”. What was two is now one new man, with no more division.

“And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross”. That is the same word as Romans 5:10, “we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son”. Reconcile means to bring together again, and the both being reconciled are the southern and northern kingdoms. So the audience in Romans is the same people God spoke to in the old covenant: the Jews in the church at Rome, and with them the Gentiles, who are the northern kingdom. Christ, by his death, brought both houses back to the Father as one.

precepts.text: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone. The stone is the King.
precepts.point: The kingdom shall not be left to other people; other races will be there, but ruling nothing. The stone is Christ, the chief cornerstone of Ephesians 2:20, and he will break these empires in pieces at the feet.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Daniel saw “that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold”. Inquiring minds want to know who this stone is, and Paul answers: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. The chief cornerstone is the leader; that means he is the King. The stone is Christ.

“without hands” means without man's hands. “the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure.” Christ is coming to destroy these empires.

And where does the stone hit? It “smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.” That is Edom's Achilles heel. It is the promise from the beginning: “it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” The feet are the last empire, America and NATO from 1776 until today. When the stone strikes there, “the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold” are broken to pieces together and become “like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them”.

“and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.” That great mountain is God's kingdom being established, the kingdom that “shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people”. Other races will be there, but they won't be ruling a thing. We are living in the days of these kings, and what you see here is the beginning of God's kingdom. You might kill millions of us, but this truth is going to continue, because the King it is built on is the chief corner stone.

precepts.text: Woe to the rebellious children, that take counsel, but not of me, and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit. If you are not covered by God's spirit, you are covered by Satan's.
precepts.point: In time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience. Those in the churches, the masses and Islam are the children of disobedience, and Satan works in them because they keep no commandment. Do not listen to parents claiming to be holy while disobeying God's law; the way out is the law, statutes and commandments through Christ.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
“Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world”: we walked according to what everybody else in this world was doing, “according to the prince of the power of the air”, Satan, “the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. The children of disobedience are those in the churches, in the mass, in Islam, in everything, disobeying God's commandments and thinking that is the way. It is not the way. The way is God's law, statutes and commandments, through his Son Jesus the Christ.

Satan is working in our people in the world, because they are not keeping any commandment. So do not listen to your parents talking about how holy they are. Satan is dealing with them, because they are the children of disobedience. How do you disobey God's commandments and call yourself holy?

Isaiah says the same: “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin”. They take counsel, but not of God. They cover with a covering, but not of his spirit.

So if you are not covered with God's spirit, whose spirit are you covered by? Satan's. The rebellious children and the children of disobedience are the same, covered by the prince of the power of the air. The only way out is to come under the covering of God's spirit by keeping his law, statutes and commandments through Christ.

precepts.text: For a long season Israel hath been without the true God, without a teaching priest and without law. Asa gathered Judah and Benjamin and the strangers with them out of Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon.
precepts.point: That is why there should be no Christian church: Christ died only for Israel. Everything they quote about Gentiles and the world has already been shown to be Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Paul writes to the saints at Ephesus, and the saints are the children of Israel. Yet he tells them, “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision”. In time past the saints were called Gentiles. They were uncircumcised in the flesh because they had been walking “according to the course of this world”, raised in pagan customs, in idolatry. The Circumcision, cut in the flesh made by hands, is the southern kingdom.

“That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world”. That sounds like Chronicles: “Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.”

Who were they? “And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.” The strangers are Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon: the northern kingdom.

An alien is a stranger, a foreigner, the way they call migrants illegal aliens today. The ten tribes became aliens to the covenant, no longer part of the commonwealth of Israel, the nation, because they were cast off. The Lord told the northern kingdom, you are not my people, and I will not be your God: without God in the world. Those are the strangers Paul says are “no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints”. The northern kingdom got its citizenship back.

precepts.text: The promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off.
precepts.point: That is why there should be no Christian church: Christ died only for Israel. Everything they quote about Gentiles and the world has already been shown to be Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who is far off? Peter answers it on the day of Pentecost: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call.”

The promise is to those Peter spoke to, to their children, and to all that are afar off. The far off are the ones who were cast off, the strangers of the northern kingdom scattered away from the land and the covenant.

So when Paul says Christ “came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh”, it is the same promise Peter preached. Christ taught the woman at the well and he taught the Jews: the far off and the nigh, both brought near by his blood.

precepts.text: Confusion of faces to the men of Judah, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off.
precepts.point: That is why there should be no Christian church: Christ died only for Israel. Everything they quote about Gentiles and the world has already been shown to be Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Who are the far off and who are the near? Daniel names them in his prayer: “O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them”.

Unto all Israel, that are near and that are far off. Both the near and the far off are Israel, driven through all the countries because of their trespass.

So when Ephesians says “ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ”, the far off are not the nations; they are Israel. Christ “hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”, abolishing the enmity, the hatred between the southern and northern kingdoms, “for to make in himself of twain one new man”. Twain means two; the one new man is Israel, all twelve reconciled. “For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.”

precepts.text: Let not the son of the stranger that hath joined himself to the Lord say, The Lord hath utterly separated me from his people. The Lord which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him beside those that are gathered: the other sheep.
precepts.point: That is why there should be no Christian church: Christ died only for Israel. Everything they quote about Gentiles and the world has already been shown to be Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Isaiah 56 ties directly into Ephesians 2. The context is “my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed”: that is Christ.

“Neither let the son of the stranger, that hath joined himself to the Lord, speak, saying, The Lord hath utterly separated me from his people”. Who is that? The northern kingdom, the one the Lord cut off and called not his people. “neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree”: they could not bring forth children.

“Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the Lord, to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant; Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer”. They say this means heathen will go into his house, and they will point to “an house of prayer for all people”. But read the next verse: “The Lord God which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him.”

The others are the other sheep: Christ said, I have other sheep not of this fold. Those gathered are this fold, and the others are the “all people” of the verse before. The son of the stranger in Isaiah 56 is the same as the strangers from the covenants of promise in Ephesians 2, who said the Lord had cut them off from his people. Now, in Christ, they are made nigh, grafted back in with their brothers, the natural branches.

precepts.text: You hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins.
precepts.point: A sister leaving her husband to stay with a mother or aunt in the world is Satan's chess move. Seek believers who can build you up.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
Christ sent Paul “To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins”. These are the people we are fighting for. Our job is to open the eyes of our people and bring them back to the light, to the commandments, and to the knowledge of who God is: Christ is a black man, he died only for the nation of Israel, and he will return for Israel alone.

Our people are in a state of darkness, and Paul says what that state is: “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world”. Our people are dead because they destroyed themselves by breaking God's commandments. They are in a state of death, without conscience, bound by Satan. Whatever the world offers, that is what they follow after.

So when you look at your mother, your uncle, your auntie inside these religions, they are bound by Satan. That is why a sister who separates from her husband and goes to her mother's house, her aunt's house or a friend's house in the world is making Satan's move. What is your mom going to teach you? She is not awake out of this dark place. Leaving a sister in the truth to live with an aunt in the world is a good chess move by Satan, and if you're not wise you won't catch it. Go to the believers who can guide you, teach you and build you up.

Will Smith reached the end of money and fame and found it could not make him happy: a man in pain, crying for help, whose soul is damaged. That is the course of this world. The dead must be quickened, and the pattern to follow is the fruit of the Spirit, meditating in the word, fasting and praying, and examining yourselves whether ye be in the faith.

precepts.text: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon. The strangers out of Ephraim and Manasseh. Northern kingdom, they were called strangers.
precepts.point: Strangers. Strangers. Now, the literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab. That does not make any sense. But when you are dealing with Christianity, it makes all the sense in the world.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Paul says “at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise”. Who were the strangers? Chronicles shows it: Asa “gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.”

The strangers out of Ephraim and Manasseh. That is the northern kingdom, and they were called strangers. Israelites, called strangers.

The literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab? That does not make any sense. It only makes sense in Christianity. But when you read that Israelites of the northern kingdom were called strangers, Ephesians 2:12 makes sense: the strangers were Israel.

precepts.text: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone. So at one point northern kingdom were not a part of the commonwealth of Israel. Why? They became strangers. They became alienated from the commonwealth of Israel. Very basic and simple. All you have to do is read. Blessed is he that readeth.
precepts.point: Strangers. Strangers. Now, the literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab. That does not make any sense. But when you are dealing with Christianity, it makes all the sense in the world.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Why were Ephraim and the northern kingdom called strangers? Hosea says it: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.”

So at one point the northern kingdom was not a part of the commonwealth of Israel. Why? Ephraim joined himself to idols and was let alone. They became strangers; they became alienated from the commonwealth of Israel. That is what Paul means by “aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”: not another race of people, but Israelites who were cut off for their idolatry.

It is very basic and simple. All you have to do is read. Blessed is he that readeth.

precepts.text: Then he said unto me, Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts. They said no hope. So Israel was without hope. We are cut off for our parts. We are alienated from the commonwealth.
precepts.point: Strangers. Strangers. Now, the literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab. That does not make any sense. But when you are dealing with Christianity, it makes all the sense in the world.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Paul says they were “having no hope, and without God in the world.” Who was without hope? Ezekiel shows it: “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts.”

They said it themselves: no hope. So Israel was the one without hope. “we are cut off for our parts”: we were alienated from the commonwealth. The dry bones are the whole house of Israel, not another nation.

So every part of Ephesians 2:12 lines up with Israel. The ones cut off, the ones with their hope lost, the aliens from the commonwealth, were the house of Israel itself, and that is who the letter is speaking to.

precepts.text: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises. To whom pertaineth the adoption, meaning the coming back, they were brought back. And the covenants. The covenants, the old and the new, only belong to the Israelites. You were strangers from the covenants of promise for a time, but it was always for you.
precepts.point: Strangers. Strangers. Now, the literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab. That does not make any sense. But when you are dealing with Christianity, it makes all the sense in the world.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Paul says the same people were “strangers from the covenants of promise”. But to whom do the covenants belong? Romans says it: they “are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”.

“to whom pertaineth the adoption”: that means the coming back; they were brought back. “and the covenants”: the covenants, the old and the new, only belong to the Israelites. The promises belong to them too.

So you can only be a stranger from a covenant that was yours to begin with. You were strangers from the covenants of promise for a time, but it was always for you. Ephesians 2:12 is Israel cut off and then brought back through Christ, not the nations being added in.

precepts.text: O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee. That are where? And that are far off. To Israel that is near and that is far off. And it says that now we are made nigh to Christ Jesus.
precepts.point: Who was far off? Who was once close and then got distant, pushed away, cut off?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Ephesians 2:13 says “ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who was far off? Who was once close, and then got distant, pushed away, cut off? Daniel answers it in his prayer.

“O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.” That are where? That are far off. The far off are Israel, driven into all the countries because of their trespass against the Lord.

So the far off of Ephesians are not other nations. They are Israel, both near and far off. Israel said, we are cut off for our parts, we have no hope. But now they do have hope, through Christ: the ones who were far off are made nigh by his blood.

precepts.text: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all. One king. Christ. And they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all. No more two nations. He hath made both one. Both one. They shall no longer be two nations. Northern kingdom, southern kingdom. Jew, Gentile. Circumcision, uncircumcision. And when those two kingdoms were against each other, they were at odds. But he said there is going to be peace.
precepts.point: Who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us. You have to know history, because why does it say both? Is it talking about just Jews and Gentiles? Why is it saying both? What happened in the history?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
“For he is our peace, who hath made both one.” He is the peace of the saints Paul writes to in Ephesians 1:1. You have to know history to understand this verse, because why does it say both? Is it only talking about Jews and Gentiles? What happened in the history?

Ezekiel shows it: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” One king: Christ. No more two nations.

That is the both that he made one: the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. Jew and Gentile, circumcision and uncircumcision, are those same two kingdoms. When those two kingdoms were against each other they were at odds, and that hatred was the middle wall of partition. But the Lord said there is going to be peace, and Christ is that peace, making the two into one again.

precepts.text: Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them. A covenant of peace with them. Ephesians 2:14 says, for he is our peace, who hath made both one. So in one chapter we are getting all of the information, all of the understanding.
precepts.point: Who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us. You have to know history, because why does it say both? Is it talking about just Jews and Gentiles? Why is it saying both? What happened in the history?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
“Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.”

This is the same chapter where the Lord promises to make the two kingdoms one nation with one king. With that promise comes a covenant of peace. And Ephesians 2:14 says, “For he is our peace, who hath made both one.” The covenant of peace Ezekiel spoke of is Christ.

So in one chapter of Ezekiel we get all of the information and all of the understanding of Ephesians 2: the two kingdoms made one, one king over them all, and an everlasting covenant of peace. Paul is not speaking about the other nations joining Israel; he is speaking about the fulfilling of this prophecy for the house of Israel.

precepts.text: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation. Carnal ordinances. So these are the commandments contained in ordinances. The law of sacrifice. That was the enmity. That was the wall of partition between them.
precepts.point: What are those commandments that are contained in ordinances? What is that talking about?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Ephesians 2:14 speaks of “the middle wall of partition between us.” What is that wall? The next verse explains it: “Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances.” A Christian’s head just blew off. They do not know what that is talking about. What are those commandments contained in ordinances?

Hebrews tells us. The tabernacle service “was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.”

Carnal ordinances. These are the commandments contained in ordinances: the law of sacrifice. That was the enmity, and that was the wall of partition between the two kingdoms. It was imposed only until the time of reformation, and Christ abolished it in his flesh, so that there is no more fighting over where and how to sacrifice.

precepts.text: And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen. All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes. He made the world for the Israelites' sake. As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle: and hast likened the abundance of them unto a drop that falleth from a vessel. That they are nothing. Does that sound like we are on friendly terms? Does that sound like friendly relations? No, they never were. It says the same thing in Isaiah 40:17, in case you do not think that the Apocrypha is canon.
precepts.point: So reconcile means to restore friendly relations. I have a question. When was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Ephesians says he made “of twain one new man, so making peace,” the same twain made one in Ezekiel 37, and the peace is the covenant of peace of Ezekiel 37:26. Then: “that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross.” Words are important, Christians; the Bible is full of them. Reconcile is a verb that means to restore friendly relations. So when was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

Ezra answers: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen. All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes.” He made the world for the Israelites’ sake.

“As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle: and hast likened the abundance of them unto a drop that falleth from a vessel.” They are nothing. Does that sound like friendly relations? No, they never were. Isaiah 40:17 says the same thing, for anyone who does not think the Apocrypha is canon. So the reconciling of Ephesians 2 cannot be about the other nations.

precepts.text: Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting. Reconciled. Reconciled who? To what? Married people get reconciled. They were together under a covenant. Something happened. They broke apart. And then, in order to bring the marriage back together, they must reconcile. That is what that means. The nation of Israel was once together under God. Something happened. Then Christ brought them back together.
precepts.point: So reconcile means to restore friendly relations. I have a question. When was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
“Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting.” The Lord is Israel’s father and Israel’s redeemer, from everlasting.

Reconciled: reconciled who, to what? Married people get reconciled. They were together under a covenant, something happened and they broke apart, and in order to bring the marriage back together they must reconcile. That is what the word means.

The nation of Israel was once together under God, as the children of their father. Something happened: sin and the split of the kingdoms. Then Christ brought them back together. That is why Ephesians says he might “reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross”: both kingdoms brought back to the Father who was always theirs.

precepts.text: We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name. We are thine. Thou never barest rule over them. God never bore rule over the other nations. So how can you reconcile to a God that never owned you, that never knew you, that never had you?
precepts.point: So reconcile means to restore friendly relations. I have a question. When was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
“We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name.” Israel says to the Lord, we are yours. And of the other nations: the Lord never bore rule over them, and they were not called by His name.

So how can anyone be reconciled to a God that never owned them, never knew them, and never had them? To reconcile is to restore friendly relations that were there before. Israel was the Lord’s, called by His name, and fell away; the other nations never were His.

That is why the reconciling of Ephesians 2:16, “that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross,” belongs to Israel. The both are the two houses of Israel, the ones called by His name, brought back to the God who bore rule over them.

precepts.text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy. So seventy weeks are determined upon thy people, the Israelites, and upon thy holy city, Jerusalem. And to make reconciliation for iniquity. So Christ dying brought reconciliation to God's people. It is very easy, very simple, very plain.
precepts.point: So reconcile means to restore friendly relations. I have a question. When was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

Thy people are the Israelites, and thy holy city is Jerusalem. Within those seventy weeks the Lord would make an end of sins and “make reconciliation for iniquity.” That reconciliation was determined upon Daniel’s people, not upon the other nations.

So when Ephesians says Christ came to “reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby,” it is the fulfilling of Daniel. Christ dying brought reconciliation to God’s people, Israel. It is very easy, very simple, very plain.

precepts.text: You hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; God, who is rich in mercy, even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ; by grace ye are saved.
precepts.point: By grace ye are saved means all of us deserve death for our sins, but through Christ we have grace and are saved from the destruction to come, if we endure to the end keeping the commandments.

note.label: Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering

precepts.why:
Paul was a master of the law, and trespass in his letters goes back to this law of the trespass offering: “you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”.
